nom: T.N. Dickinson's Witch Hazel Moisturizing Astringent

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin, including one who reaches for the alcohol version specifically in summer when her face gets oilier, say it gives a clean, refreshing feel and helps balance oil in shine-prone areas.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin, including one who calls her skin "really sensitive dry skin," report the alcohol-free version does not dry their skin out further and works well in small amounts.
segments.combination: Several reviewers with combination skin use it as a daily toner after cleansing, saying it removes leftover oil and dirt without leaving skin tight or dry and helps calm redness; one notes it works especially well in months her skin runs oilier.
segments.sensitive: Most reviewers with sensitive skin say the alcohol-free version is the one witch hazel that doesn't irritate their skin, leaving it clean and calm without dryness; one dissenting review cautions that witch hazel is strong and sensitive-skin users need to be careful how they use it.
segments.mature: A couple of reviewers in their 50s and 70s say it has been a long-standing, dependable part of their facial routine, with one 70-year-old crediting it for compliments on her skin over decades of use.

concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers, especially with the alcohol-free version, say it hydrates and leaves skin soft without tightness or stripping, some crediting the added aloe and hyaluronic acid; one dissenting review notes her skin felt slightly drier in colder months and needed a moisturizer layered on top.
concerns.redness: A couple of reviewers say it calms facial redness and feels soothing when used as a toner.
concerns.spots: One reviewer says it helps even out her skin tone when used each morning before makeup.
concerns.blemishes: A couple of reviewers use it as a spot treatment directly on blemishes, saying breakouts shrink down and calm faster than usual with regular dabbing.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily skin say it removes excess oil and leaves a clean, refreshing, balanced feel, particularly during months or seasons when their skin runs oilier.

aspects.libelle: Strong, medicinal scent for some users

Large bottle, strong value for the price
Newer formula adds preservatives to the label
Alcohol-free version feels gentler than original
Can sting on freshly shaved or broken skin

extraits.texte: This product label says”made with 100% natural witch hazel”. I believed that it meant the only ingredient was witch hazel The last time that I bought this brand , it was the only ingredient. They have now added 6 preservatives/ingredients. They are tricking you into thinking that’s all that’s in it. I didn’t want anyone else to get tricked. It was too late to return when I read the back of the bottle
The witch hazel is very strong, so you have to be careful when using it, especially on sensitive skin. However, it works well and leaves the skin feeling clean and refreshed when used properly.

extraits.titre: One of the things I would want with me if I was stuck on a desert island!
extraits.texte: No sting, no alcohol, no bad smell, soothing and pure. This is my go-to face wash and the only thing I have washed my face with since I was 14. I am 70 and witch hazel has taken good care of my facial skin. People tell me how nice my skin is and attribute it to witch hazel - especially this brand. It is my favorite because you can choose between alchohol free or not, because of the scent (or rather the lack of) and the little bit of aloe vera and hyaluronic acid. I use the one with alchohol in the summer when my face is a bit more oily and it gives a clean refreshing feeling. I also mix with a bit of peppermint and tea tree oil in a small spray bottle for a refreshing cooling facial spritz (i started this when my hot flashes started and it is very cooling!) I also like this for cleaning and soothing certain personal areas and for a nice scalp refresher. Sometimes i will mix with a rose essential oil or any other essential oil that has a nice scent and use as a freshening spray when I am at the beach or at a special occasion. Love this stuff and especially this brand! It arrived fast (next day). This is my favorite beauty and personal product - one of the 3 things I would choose to have if i was stuck on a desert island! The soothing properties are a must and it has many uses!

extraits.titre: Simple ingredients, no unnecessary extras, and exactly what witch hazel should be.
extraits.texte: I'm 50 with sensitive skin, and this has become a permanent part of both my morning and evening skincare routines. One of the biggest reasons I keep buying it is the ingredient list. I appreciate that it doesn't have a bunch of unnecessary extras. It's alcohol-free, fragrance-free, and contains ingredients that actually benefit my skin instead of potentially irritating it. I also love that it smells like real witch hazel, not alcohol. If you've ever used those harsh astringents that leave your eyes watering, this is the complete opposite. The scent is clean and natural, and it never leaves my skin feeling tight or stripped. I use it after Pond's Cold Cream, allowing it to dry completely before applying the next step in my routine. It leaves my skin feeling fresh, balanced, and ready for whatever comes next. It's one of those products that quietly does its job every single day without any drama, and I think that's exactly what good skincare should do. This has become a staple in my routine, and I'll continue repurchasing it.

I wasn’t expecting to fall in love with a bottle of witch hazel, but here we are. I’ve been using T.N. Dickinson’s Witch Hazel for a few weeks now, and my skin has honestly never looked better. I have combination skin that leans oily, and this has been perfect as a toner after cleansing. It removes leftover dirt and oil without making my skin feel tight or dry. It’s also been a lifesaver during breakouts — I dab a little directly on blemishes, and they shrink down way faster than usual. The scent is natural and a bit medicinal (which I actually like — it smells clean and simple, not overly perfumed). I also started using it after shaving and on little bug bites or razor bumps, and it’s so soothing. It’s one of those old-school, multi-use products that actually delivers.

I’ve been using witch hazel twice a day—once in the morning and once at night—after cleansing my face. It leaves my skin feeling refreshed and clean without any residue. I’ve also used it to calm down breakouts, and it works wonders as a spot treatment. However, I did notice that during colder months, my skin felt slightly drier, so I had to follow up with a good moisturizer. Overall, I highly recommend witch hazel for anyone looking for a natural, affordable, and effective skincare product. It’s especially great for those with oily or combination skin, but even sensitive skin types can benefit if you choose an alcohol-free formula. While it’s not a miracle worker, it’s a reliable addition to any skincare routine. I’d give it a 5 stars.
